samples.text: Heading up alongside Estonia, the Global Dialogue on Artificial Intelligence Governance, El Salvador reaffirmed that this technology must expand capacities and create opportunities to build environments that can be competitive in the future. Mr. President, the transformation that my country is experiencing has shown us that security, development and human dignity are not separate files. The fact is that without security, development is fragile. Without development, it's very difficult to make security sustainable. And without dignity, neither of these things make any sense. The international community must understand that resolving these challenges, these global challenges, goes above and beyond, well beyond actually, any resolutions, millions of resolutions on paper. multilateralism that does not oblige countries to constantly choose between sovereignty and cooperation. Today, we have an historical and inexcusable challenge, and that is making multilateralism a synonym, again, with capacity to act. El Salvador believes that the reform of the United Nations should not be restricted to reorganizing its structures. We need an organization that is agile, representative, effective, and transparent, that's able to resolve contemporary challenges with the speed required. So enough with the conformism, enough of personal and national interests prevailing over the needs of the world and global crises. And enough, ladies and gentlemen, enough with the bureaucracy. Let us hope that the next Secretary General of the United Nations is able to show leadership with absolute full independence and ability to engage in dialogue, moral authority, knowledge of the international reality, and that they have a willingness to reform and a conviction that we need to reform to benefit humanity, like my President Bukele, regardless of the consequences. Because one human life is worth it, just a single life. is worth the effort. El Salvador, in a short but historic period of seven years, made strong strides forward to change our reality, recovering our security, our spaces, trust, dignity. However, we did this while always fighting to safeguard our sovereignty, because our sovereignty is not up for negotiation. Our sovereignty is not, must not be touched.

cross borders, its money moves through international financial systems and its networks operate across numerous countries. I will do everything necessary to combat that scourge, but a transnational threat requires the international community to play its part as well. Security, while essential, is not enough. A territory that provides no opportunities remains vulnerable. My administration is therefore also focused on ensuring that Colombia grows again. For years, we have discussed how to better distribute what we have. That is a legitimate, necessary discussion, but it's absolutely not enough. We also need to ask ourselves, how are we going to produce more? In the end, Governments can't decree economic growth. What they have to do is lay the foundations for it to occur. In our miracle nation, we want an idea to be able to become a business, a business to create jobs and for jobs to become well-being for our people. To those of you anywhere else in the world who are wondering where to invest, I would like to invite you to look at Colombia. It's a country with access to two oceans, productive land, energy resources, enormous biodiversity, an excellent geographical position, and a government that champions private enterprise. But above all, look at our people. Colombia does not want to watch the technological transformation of our time from the sidelines. We want to be a part of it. We want to train young people for super intelligence, for robotics, for data science, for agro industry, for engineering, and for the new economy. Millions of Colombians are not asking the state to sought out their lives, they're asking the state to give them the opportunity to build those lives. And that is what gives meaning to what I have called the miracle nation. This isn't the name of a government. nor is it a naive promise that our problems will just disappear. No, that's not it. This is the country that we're going to build.

This is an automated review, never a claim of human verification. Read every representative and boundary passage. Propose analytical theme definitions grounded in these statements. Separate technical AI safety from military/security concerns when warranted. Include minority positions; do not force one theme per cluster or a predetermined number. Every theme needs exact source examples, inclusion/exclusion and boundary cases.
